topHook: Coke cost 5¢ for 73 years. Here's why.

scenes.vo: [calm, curious] For seventy-three years, a Coke cost exactly one nickel.
scenes.label: a bottle of Coke, 1886–1959

scenes.vo: Wars. The Great Depression. Still five cents.
Why? Coca-Cola's vending machines only took one coin.
[lowered] So when costs went up, what could Coke do?
In 1953, it asked the US Treasury to make a new coin. Seven and a half cents.
scenes.label: the coin Coca-Cola asked for

scenes.vo: So Coke planned something stranger. One in every nine bottles from its machines would come out empty.
scenes.label: bottles planned to be empty

scenes.vo: [quiet, knowing] Seventy-three years, decided by the size of one coin. Which is why
